chapters.title: Chapter 1: awakening
chapters.html:
It wouldn't be true to say that Phainon was not struggling, but it would also be true that he was, in fact, struggling.

He was used to fighting off the monsters. The monsters were getting stronger day by day, therefore it was safe to say that he might be struggling, not that he would admit that out loud.

Thanks to Lady Tribbie they landed safely. With the monsters closing on Okhema, Lady Aglaea could only send Mydei and him. They were the best warriors of the Chrysos Heirs.

Mydei looked fine on the outside but Phainon knew better. His eyebrows were slightly furrowed and sweat was dripping down his forehead. Well, they were fighting for nearly 5 hours without rest so that was understandable.

What was not understandable to him was why Mydei was suddenly looking at him with such anxiety. He admits, he was not at his finest condition per se, but he wasn't looking that bad, was he?

With confusion clouding his mind he didn’t notice the monster behind him until it struck, hitting with such force that he stumbled across the battlefield. Among the sounds of fighting, he thought he heard Mydei yell his name, though he wasn’t certain it was real or just a figment of his imagination.

He felt himself falling onto the hard ground then his consciousness was slipping away, but before that he felt someone's touch on his skin. He assumed that was Mydei, cause otherwise he was fucked.

Assuming that it was Mydei, for some reason his vision was slowly darkening, he said “I guess this round is yours.” just as he finished his sentence, he passed out.

* * *

Upon waking up he felt as if he was sleeping for years. He tried to raise his head, but dizziness forced him back. Deciding it was useless to get up just yet, he focused on his surroundings.

He was in some white room... or so it seemed. He didn't recognize the room but he figured it was a hospital by the smell of the disinfectants. Now the only question is why was he in a hospital (probably something to do with his head ‘cause it was starting to hurt) and why didn't he remember what happened?

While he was drowning in his thoughts, his room's door was opened by some short pink haired lady.

“Ah, you're finally awake, Lord Phainon! Lady Aglaea was starting to worry about you.” she said smiling. But his gaze must have felt off ‘cause she furrowed her brows as if she could figure it out by just looking intensively.

“Is everything okay?”

“Uhm, yeah although my head is kinda killing me so if you can do something about that it would be much appreciated Miss…?” said Phainon sheepishly, scratching the back of his head.

She looked confused. So, his head wasn't supposed to hurt, Phainon deduced.


“Is that a bad sign, Miss…? Sorry, could I have your name? Haha, you know mine, but I don’t know yours—it’s not fair.” he said jokingly. Now she looked really worried.

“Don’t you know who I am, Lord Phainon?” she asked hesitantly. It was as if the answer frightened her.

“Uhm, sorry Miss but I don't remember meeting you before.” Just as he answered her he realized something “In fact.. I don't remember anything..?”

what was happening?

“What's going on?” Now he was also scared. The pink haired lady must have come to an understanding of the situation because she looked as if she had an idea of what was happening.

“Oh, well before that I must ask you some questions just to be sure, is that okay?” She told him with a reassuring smile on her face. “Okay.”

At that moment, a few people came into his room. There were three red haired children? Must be triplets, they were almost identical.

After them came some cyan haired man with an eyepatch on his left eye. He looked exasperated by something and was kind of intimidating looking.

Following them came a very elegant looking lady. She had golden hair, also golden attire. She looked really majestic to be honest. Seeing as Phainon was looking at her she smiled.

“Good morning Phainon, glad to see you woken up. How are you feeling?” Not knowing how to answer the question he looked at the pink haired lady.

“Hello, Lady Aglaea. I was just about to confirm something. I hope I'm wrong but you might wanna wait for a moment.” The pink haired lady said while looking at Phainon. Without letting her ask any question she spoke

“Well, lets start now. Do you know your name?” She paused. “Like did you know before I addressed you with it?”

“Yes. I knew that. My name is Phainon.”

“Do you know where you're from?” Phainon paused. Phainon tried to think, but nothing came. Pain throbbed in his head, sharper than before

“No,” he said reluctantly. “I don't remember.” he said with worry in his voice. He was also holding his head.

The man with an eyepatch was looking kind of intrigued. He then asks, “What’s the last thing you remember?”

Phainon thinks the question is an easy one, but when he tried to think, he couldn't remember, he didn't remember. Which was very scary, so he tried very hard to remember. Surely there was something he could remember?

His headache was getting more intense; he felt as if he was slipping from reality. There was some motion next to his bed but he remembered something. As darkness claimed him, a single word escaped his lips:

“Mydeimos.”

chapters.title: Chapter 2: first encounter again
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

familiar strangers, or so

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Fighting back and forth, Mydei knocked more enemies as he made his surroundings more clear. His gauntlet was stained with the blood of the monsters. No matter how much they slained, they just kept coming. He wasn't sure how much longer Phainon and he could manage.

As if they heard his thoughts, the horde of monsters started closing in. Normally, they could handle it. What are a few more monsters for them? But they were fighting for almost 5 hours, so It wouldn’t be wrong to say that he was nearing the end of his strength.

He glanced around the battlefield, trying to see how Phainon was doing. As expected, he was also looking tired but something was amiss. It was like he didn't realize the monsters were closing on him, which was weird even though he always says to Phainon he never notices his surroundings, normally, that didn’t apply in battles.

At that moment Phainon also looked at him. He probably saw the confusion in his face 'cause now he was looking curious. 

Before Mydei could react, a monster appeared from nowhere behind Phainon and struck him. Phainon stumbled and fell. Hard. 

Slashing through the monsters, Mydei made his way to him. Seeing him up close, Mydei realized just how battered Phainon was—bloodied, bruised, and barely standing. They needed to get out of here. Quickly. 

He looked at Mydei with uncertainty, as if second-guessing himself, before finally speaking;

“I guess this round is yours.”

Mydei looked bewildered at Phainon. He let out a soft chuckle to himself and hoisted him onto his back. “As if that was ever in question.” 

                                      * * *

Carrying Phainon was not a new development. Although usually he wasn't in such bad shape, as he was now.

As he got closer to Okhema, he saw Hyacine helping someone. But as soon as her eyes made contact with him, she said something quickly to the man beside her, who nodded in response then rushed over to examine Phainon carefully. 

She did some first aid and hurriedly told him to bring him to her clinic. “Dei, quickly carry him. He is not looking very good right now.” She told Mydei very tensely, he nodded at her.

After carrying him inside she healed his major injuries, Phainon no longer looked on the verge of death, which was a relief—Mydei never wanted to see him like that again. Then Mydei released the breath he didn't know he was holding.

“He needs rest right now but other than that he's okay,” After a tense few moments, she leaned back, relief softening her face. “Just to be sure I need to examine him again when he wakes up to see if there was any damage,” She smiled at him. 

“He probably won't wake up for another 3 days so you go and take a rest.”

“I'm fine.”

“If you want to sleep next door to Phainon I can make that happen,” She gave him a smile that carried a clear hint of threat.

“Go home Dei, and I better not see you until tomorrow. No excuses, go.” Without letting him speak, Hyacine goes to see the next patient.

Mydei huffed, then looked back at Phainon. Mydei was fine and didn't need ‘rest’ but he did not want to be the victim of Hyacine’s wrath. With one last look, he exited the room. 

                                         * * *

When Phainon woke up, this time he knew where he was. He actually remembered, no pun intended. He was also alone this time, so that gave him some time to think.

The last thing he recalled was calling out a name. Mydeimos? What kind of name was that? Right after that, he must have passed out from the pain in his head—he assumed it was because of his injury.

He tried to remember more, but nothing came to his mind except the moment when he had woken up here, which he guessed was a couple of hours ago.

Wanting to get up, he tested whether he could sit. He couldn't manage it, but at least the pain was duller now. He wondered what could have possibly happened to make him lose his memories?

While he was deep in thought (It seemed this kept happening to him.) There was a knock on the door, then the door opened.

A tall man was standing at the doorway. A tall man with golden hair and red tattoos all over his… chest? (Was he naked?) He looked intimidating but not like the cyan-haired dude. (Also, calling the cyan-haired man dude, even in his mind, made him shiver for some reason. Weird, he didn't remember anything but his body apparently did.)

This man looked familiar—now this was a first. Phainon thought he must be someone important to him. He felt a warm feeling in his chest.

The man did not speak. Phainon took that as a challenge and he decided not to speak as well. (This felt so familiar.)

After a minute or two, it looked like the man settled on accepting his defeat. He sighed, then spoke,

“Deliverer.”

He would have liked to have the upper hand, but clearly he couldn’t—thanks to his memory loss.

“Uhh, I suppose that is a title of mine?”

The man grunted, and Phainon took offence to that.

“It’s not my fault I lost my memory? Wait, no I don't know that. It's not my fault that I don't remember. This also doesn't sound right. Ughh whatever don't hold me responsible for the things I don't remember, okay?” He said, rather pathetically, if he might add.

The man looked… amused? Phainon felt both irritated and pleased.

“It seems memory loss doesn't change much for you, after all you still act like an idiot.” The man said very rudely, if Phainon might add.

“It's not nice to pick on people who just wake up, you know? Who are you anyway?” Phainon said, trying to seem not interested but he was failing miserably, apparently, because the man saw right through him. He smirked and spoke,

“My name is Mydei, short for Mydeimos,” Phainon looked intrigued. (Who wouldn't be? After all that was the only name he remembered.) “I am also curious about what you remember,

so let's talk.”

Phainon thought his day was going ironically well.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 3: names and lies
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

is home still home if you don't remember it?

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

“Alright. First question—why are you naked?” Phainon asked rather shamelessly, it had been bugging him the moment he saw him. It was winter for Titan’s sake, he was literally freezing. Besides, he was sure that there had to be some rules against it.

Mydei (short for Mydeimos) just stared at him blankly, as if this were the first time anyone had ever dared to ask. Which was ridiculous—anyone with eyes could see he was, well, basically naked.

“This is the first thing you want to ask me?” His stare didn't waver. Now, Phainon was starting to doubt himself but he still needed to know. He had to know whether this man had a disease or just liked walking around naked.

After a solid fifteen seconds of silence, Mydei sighed, as though dealing with a troublesome child.

“First of all, I am not naked. Stop exaggerating. Second, this is how we Kremnoans present ourselves.” said Mydei with a clipped tone but looking very much proud of his culture.

So it was a cultural thing, Phainon thought. Weird to him, sure, but who is he to judge?

“Okay. Makes sense, I guess. So—I wanted to ask, how do we know each other?”

“We are rivals. Partners. Comrades. Whatever you want to call it,” Mydei said evenly. “When we first met, I was not your ally. My people came first—and that hasn’t changed. We fought for ten days straight. Neither of us won, but I respected your will to protect. So we called it a tie. Also… I am the Prince of Castrum Kremnos.” He said hesitantly, not sure if he should've said it or not.

At that moment, piercing pain struck him on his head. Mydei quickly rushed over to him, checking what's wrong.

“Are you okay?” Mydei asked with a grim expression on his face. He probably looked worse than he felt.

“I'm fine, don't worry it lasted only a second.”
“Was it because of what I said?” Mydei asked white-haired patient, feeling somewhat guilty.

As if he could sense it, Phainon suddenly looked at him very seriously.

“No. It's not your fault that I lost my memories so don't feel guilty about it.”

“Who said I was guilty?” said Mydei, refusing the accusation even if it held a little truth. But no one had to know that.

Phainon rolled his eyes, figuring out that the man next to him didn't want to talk about his feelings, he decided not to talk about it. (But they will some day, it's just postponed, that's all.)

“Anyways, I wanna go outside. I'm bored out of my mind and I feel fine. There is no point in me occupying numbered beds. Can you accompany me? I feel as if we do that sometimes.”

Something flashed between Mydei’s eyes. As if he recalled something, but it disappeared quickly.

“I suppose I have some time to kill.”

* * *
As he walked through the streets of Okhema, nothing felt familiar to him. He thought maybe, just maybe something could seem familiar, but nothing did.

The only thing that was slightly familiar to him was bickering with Mydei, which felt like second nature.

“I'm just saying, how convenient that you remind me I lost to you 336 times when I have no recollection of it.” said Phainon, slightly annoyed, not believing anything that Mydei told him.

“I also said you won 334 of these, Deliverer. Which shows you that I am, indeed, stronger and better than you. And by the way, you can ask the witnesses of my winnings.” Mydei said, smirking. He was clearly enjoying this conversation.

While they were walking around, they started talking about their past activities — more like Mydei shared them and Phainon refused to believe them. That’s why the conversation was going like this.

"I’ll believe it when I remember it—oh wait, I don't remember! So no. And what’s with the ‘Deliverer’?” he air-quoted. “This is the second time you’ve called me that. Was I some prophet or something? Or a simple delivery man?"

Suddenly, Mydei stopped walking, semingly remembered something. Phainon didn't notice any of it, too busy watching the people of Okhema city. He looked like a child wandering around in a town for the first time. It could be somewhat true for Phainon, it is his first time that he remembers after all.

Mydei stubbornly didn't look at Phainon as he spoke, as if it was hurting him to see him like this.

“You are not a prophet or a delivery man. It is a title, yes, but it does not hold any meaning. It is my nickname for you.”

It technically wasn’t a lie—he wasn’t a prophet. And this amnesic Phainon didn’t need to know the cruelty of the world yet; seeing that Phainon looked better without worry. Maybe it wasn’t right what Mydei was doing, but he didn’t feel bad about it.

“Oh,” Phainon said, clearly disappointed. Even if he didn’t remember a thing, he felt like he was somewhat important. When he woke up, he was addressed as Lord Phainon. Even if he felt embarrassed by the title, he didn't feel strange hearing it.

Still, it was too early to talk about things he had no knowledge of, so he didn't comment on how that felt like a lie.

“I see. Well if you say so.”

Mydei wasn’t expecting a disagreement, sure. But watching Phainon say that without any emotion felt wrong.

At the same time, Phainon wondered whether trusting Mydei was the right call.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 4: dream or reality?
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

untouched by the hand of death, who emerges victorious?

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Having conflicted feelings about someone when you didn’t remember anything was strange.

He felt as if this man couldn’t be trusted — clearly lying and hiding things. And yet, he wanted to believe every word he said. Even without his memories, he still trusted the blond-haired prince.

As they walked in silence, a purple-haired woman approached them. Mydei looked like he recognized her, so he relaxed. Phainon wasn’t sure why he trusted him, but he followed his lead and examined the woman.

She had purple hair, purple clothes, and a flower crown on her head. There was a sweet yet dangerous aura around her. Phainon had no idea what to make of it.

Strangely enough, his body recognized her too. He knew instinctively that she wasn’t a threat.

“Hello, Lord Phainon. Lord Mydeimos,” she said, smiling at Phainon. “Lady Aglaea sent me with a message. She wants to see you at your earliest convenience.”

She kept her eyes on Phainon, clearly expecting something.

“Hi. Sorry. I’m Phainon — which you probably knew. Could you introduce yourself, please? I have some memory issues… which you also knew. Anyway— yeah.” Phainon felt embarrassed for not being able to speak properly.

He glanced at Mydei, checking for his reaction. Mydei looked amused. Insultingly amused.

Annoyance — which was becoming strangely common around Mydei — flared up, and he shot him an irritated look.

The purple-haired woman chuckled softly, amused by the interaction.

“I’m Castorice. Yes, I know you — and yes, I know about your condition. I’m just glad to see you well… aside from the memory loss.”

As soon as he heard her name, something sharp flickered behind Phainon’s eyes.

A sound.
A scent.
A flash of purple.

For a moment, Castorice’s smile blurred, replaced by another image: her crying—looking at him painfully, the night sky behind her. She was screaming his name:

“Phainon, stop this. We can find another way.”

Another voice answered her, a voice that was unmistakably his own.

“Fighting with me is futile, Castorice,” he sounded so hollow. “You don’t need to do this. Just give it to me.”

He blinked, reality reassembling around him. His breath hitched, short and shallow, as if someone had slammed a weight onto his chest.

“Lord Phainon, are you okay?” Castorice asked, concern washing over her face.

He wasn’t.
Not after what he had just seen.
But he forced a smile anyway.

“Yeah, I just—got dizzy suddenly. I felt something… like I’ve seen you before. I mean—obviously I have, but not like this. It felt like a memory. I’m not sure, though.”

He didn’t mention the details—how he had looked like her enemy, how he had sounded cold, threatening. He had no idea how to even start explaining that.

A thought struck him suddenly.
If what he saw was a memory… then she should know what it was about, right?

Hope bloomed in his chest—sharp, desperate, almost painful.

But the moment it bloomed, it withered.

Because if she didn’t know what he was talking about… then what exactly did he see?
And if she did know—why weren’t they hostile toward him? Why were they treating him gently? Cautiously? Kindly?

Unless that kindness was a tactic.
Unless this was all designed to make him lower his guard.

If so, it was already working.
Because he couldn’t be any more vulnerable than this.

Phainon’s thoughts began to swirl uncontrollably. That image—his own voice, that harsh tone, Castorice’s tear-streaked face… Nothing fit together, yet the feeling inside him was crystal clear:

He was afraid.
Of himself.

That voice…
That commanding, emotionless tone…
It was as if someone else inside him had spoken.

Even though he had lost his memories, he didn’t feel like that man, nor did he think he could sound like that… but apparently, he could.

What if he really was a terrible person? What did that memory—even if it was only a fragment—mean? Was it a dream, a nightmare… or reality?
He didn’t want it to be reality.

But he had no way of knowing until his memories returned.

———

While Phainon struggled with his thoughts, Mydei watched him silently, observing every twitch and subtle expression, trying to understand what could possibly shake him like this.

He wanted to ask, to reach out—but he didn’t know how. Mydei was a man who never lied, yet somehow the words failed him. How could he phrase a question when even he wasn’t sure what to ask?

Phainon’s chest tightened as the panic inside him refused to settle. Every breath felt heavy, every blink a reminder of the uncertainty gripping his mind.

He didn’t realize that Mydei’s gaze was measuring him—not in judgment, but in careful observation. He was watching, waiting, as if he knew that the answer Phainon sought might not come for a long while.

Mydei spoke at last, his voice low and deliberate. “Memories aren’t always the truth, Deliverer. Sometimes they’re warnings. Sometimes they’re lies. Don’t assume they dictate who you are today.”

“We will figure this out together. You will remember when you need to. There is no need to rush things, Lord Phainon. You will remember when you’re ready, both mentally and physically,” Castorice added gently.

In that shared silence, the truth became painfully clear to Phainon: he was more vulnerable than he had ever been.

“What if I’m never ready?” he asked quietly.

“You will be,” Mydei answered simply, his eyes still on Phainon. “Or at least you’ll move forward, whether ready or not.”

Phainon’s stomach twisted. The words should have comforted him, but they only deepened the knot of fear in his chest. How can he move forward if he didn't even know what he is?

For the first time, he understood that surviving this memory—or whatever it had been—was only the beginning.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 5: through fire and memory
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

confronting the past that refuses the stay buried (does he want to?)

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

After all those stressful memory recollection moments, they were finally ready to see Aglaea. Still, Phainon held doubts about himself and the others.

If he was truly their friend—or comrade—why did he have that memory of himself being emotionless, ruthless, and fearsome?

And somehow, he had the uneasy feeling that they didn’t know about that memory either, as if a part of him had been kept secret even from those closest to him.

Castorice led the way, her purple hair catching the soft light of Okhema’s streets, shimmering as it swayed with each step.

The sunlight filtered through the narrow alleyways, glinting off rooftops and cobblestones, casting patterns that danced across the walls.

Mydei walked beside him, upright and composed, yet there was a tension in his shoulders that Phainon couldn’t read. It was a subtle stiffness, almost imperceptible, but enough to set Phainon’s mind racing.

He tried to focus on other things—the sunlight glinting off rooftops, the distant chatter of townsfolk, —but his thoughts kept returning, spinning around the unanswered questions, the inconsistencies of memory, and the unease that had been growing inside him.

Probably sensing his gaze, Mydei frowned.
“Is something on my face?” he asked thoughtfully, brushing at it with the back of his hand.

“Nothing. I was just thinking how stupid you look,” Phainon lied, forcing a small, awkward smirk. Mydei didn’t need to know the truth—that it was more a reflection of his own anxious thoughts than any real judgment of Mydei’s expression.

Annoyed, Mydei let out a quiet sigh, his voice low but firm. “If you have nothing important to say, keep it to yourself, Deliverer. We should hurry—Aglaea won’t be pleased if we’re late.”

Phainon frowned. “Late? But she didn’t tell us a specific time to go, though?”

Mydei’s mocking smile only made Phainon grit his teeth slightly. “She doesn’t need to. She knows we know not to be late.”

Phainon wanted to protest, to explain that his memory was still fractured, that he had gaps no one else seemed aware of, but it would accomplish nothing. They weren’t amnesic, so he stayed silent, swallowing the words he wished he could voice.

The soft breeze ruffled Castorice’s flower crown as she led the way, petals catching the sunlight, sparkling like tiny fragments of amethyst.

Phainon’s heart thudded uneasily—not from the walking, but from the anticipation, from the invisible weight of the unknown that awaited them.

The very air seemed to vibrate with tension, every shadow hinting at a secret or warning.

———

Finally arriving at the meeting point, he braced himself to hear what Lady Aglaea wanted to discuss. His hands twitched slightly, the nerves knotting deep in his stomach, the uneasy sense of expectation pressing down on him.

“Thank you for coming so quickly at such short notice. I apologize for the sudden request, but it is an important matter to discuss,” Aglaea said calmly, her voice composed in a way that made Phainon feel almost guilty for expecting panic.

Knowing Aglaea, he understood immediately: she was not joking. She would not joke in moments like this. He didn’t need his memories to deduce that.

Every inflection, every pause carried weight; every carefully chosen word hinted at significance far beyond the mundane.

“Of course. What did you need to talk to us about?” Mydei asked, clearly impatient. There was an edge in his voice, one that suggested he valued efficiency above pleasantries.

“We discovered that yesterday was not a coincidence.”

“What do you mean?” Mydei pressed, brow furrowed.

“The day you and Phainon battled the Black Tide, it was no accident there were more monsters than expected. Someone wanted to keep you there longer,” Aglaea said, her tone heavy with seriousness.

Her eyes held a flicker of something—worry, perhaps, or fear, but she did not elaborate, leaving Phainon to grapple with unease.

Phainon’s breath caught. He didn’t remember this, yet his body reacted instinctively, tense and alert, muscles coiling like a spring ready to snap.

“Also, before heading out that day, you came to me,” she continued, each word deliberate.

Phainon froze. His body’s reaction betrayed him, though his mind grasped for understanding. He didn’t know what she meant, but his muscles tensed automatically, a primal response he could not control.

“You seemed anxious about something, as if you knew something was going to happen to you, but you didn’t know when,” she explained softly.

Phainon felt panic rising like a tide inside him; his breath quickened. He hated this vulnerability, this helplessness—relying on others to fill in the gaps of his own life, only to discover truths he should have already known.

“Your past is not lost, Lord Phainon. It waits. When you remember is very important,” Aglaea added, her calm voice concealing a layer of anxious urgency.

“But…why? Why is it important that I remember? Obviously, I care, but why…for you?” Phainon asked, his voice quivering slightly, overwhelmed by the weight of the moment.

“Because,” she paused carefully, choosing her words, “you said that someone would try to kill you. And if you forgot everything… it meant they succeeded.”

The world stopped—or perhaps it was a minute. Phainon couldn’t breathe. Pain shot through his skull as the world spun violently.

Voices clamored for his attention, opening and closing, but he couldn’t focus. He could hear mouths moving, words forming, yet they reached him not as language but as an unintelligible echo.

He passed out.

———

At first, there was only warmth. Not comforting warmth—it was suffocating, thick and pressing against his skin.

A low crackle echoed in the distance. Then the screaming began, sharp and panicked, filling the air around him.

He opened his eyes. The world was red. Aedes Elysiea was burning. He knew this place—it was his hometown. He remembered.

Heat scorched his cheeks, each breath a labor. This wasn’t random. This was his memory, unaltered, raw and vivid.

His body moved on its own, as if possessed, carrying him forward without his will.

Monsters roamed freely, chaos spreading through the village. People screamed, ran, stumbled. Destruction and fire engulfed everything.

Phainon ran toward the cries, desperate to help, desperate to change outcomes, but the sense of futility weighed heavily.

He found a child, covered in blood.

“Hey! Are you okay? Can you walk? Come on, let’s get somewhere safe. Where is your family? Never mind, safety first,” Phainon urged, panic rising in his voice.

Yet the child did not respond—or perhaps could not.

He tried again, reaching for the child’s shoulder. At the moment his hand touched the small figure, the child turned.

It was him. A younger version of himself. Mini Phainon. The sight unsettled him to his core, staring as though through him and at him at the same time.

“You cannot save them. You are always a failure. You want to be a hero? It might have been possible if you had saved your village. But you are nothing but a fake. And most importantly? This is all your fault.”

It hit him like a punch to the stomach. He collapsed to his knees. Mini Phainon continued, relentlessly.

“The day you remember will be the day everything ends. Are you sure you still want to know your past?”

The fire spread around them, circling, a ring of unrelenting destruction. The only thing untouched: Phainon. Mini Phainon’s clothes caught fire, his figure slowly disintegrating, fading into nothingness.

“You will make a choice soon. You or them. Either way, there is no good ending. I wish you luck,” the small version said, dissolving further into a black figure.

Before Phainon could react, the world shifted, shadows pulling and twisting.

The last thing he saw before consciousness returned was the black figure standing where Mini Phainon had been. Then, suddenly, he woke up.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 6: awakened nightmare
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

phainon wakes up

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Waking up felt as if he was buried in some sludge and trying to breathe. He was hearing broken, distorted voices. They weren't clear, but they were enough to understand that someone was trying to talk to him.

“Is… okay..? Why…. ing up…?”
“He… ems… to… ight.”
“He's waking up!”

The last voice was clear. It was… Hyacine? When did she get here?

“Are you alright, Snowy?” Hyacine asked with a reassuring smile. “You seemed to have passed out, so they called me. Do you have any discomfort?”

He gave himself time to think. He looked at himself first, focusing on his shoulder where his younger self had touched him in the vision. He was curious whether there was any physical sign of it being real.

He lifted his shirt a little, and there it was: a big, black mark. His vision had also worsened slightly, leaving dark spots blurring the corners of his eyes.

Finally, he found a mirror next to him. When he looked at his reflection, he… he looked like a mess. How long had it been since he looked like someone on his deathbed?

Also, his eyes… his iris had changed. There was something like a piece of the sun trapped in his iris, glowing as if it were waiting for its moment to truly shine.

The strange thing was, he didn't find it weird. It felt as though this was how it was always supposed to be. It was as if losing his memories had also cost him a piece of himself, and now, he was finally regaining it. But it raised a terrifying question: was that actually a good thing?

Before he had any time to ponder, Mydei nudged him. He looked grumpy and annoyed as usual, but that wasn't all. He was obviously worried about the current condition of the “Deliverer”.

Mydei raised one eyebrow, an unimpressed expression settling on his face. “If you're thinking that long about whether you have any discomfort or not, then you're fine. Now, tell us. What the hell happened back there?”

Phainon started to look around, only just realizing that they had changed locations. Just how long had he been unconscious? “How long was I out?”

“Nearly six hours,” Hyacine answered, a worried expression clouding her face, completely failing to hide any of her feelings.

Phainon didn’t know how to feel about his predicament. The things he had seen and felt were beyond anything he could imagine explaining. And worst of all, they weren’t unfamiliar.

“I might have seen something… I probably saw something, but,” Phainon hesitated, “I don’t remember it.” Catching the heavy frown tightening Mydei’s features, Phainon quickly turned his head away, unable to hold that sharp gaze.

Unconsciously, he tried to bury the reality of what he had witnessed. He remembered the dream—every terrifying second of it—but admitting that was out of the question. How could he, when everything he saw explained nothing and only added new questions?

“What do you mean?” Hyacine asked, her brows furrowing. It was an unusual sight; Hyacine almost always had a smile on her face.

“Like I said, I don't remember a thing. All I know is that it was not good.” It was a lie hidden within the truth. He didn’t want to lie, but what choice did he have when all he could gather from those memories was that he was not the person he, and his friends, thought he was?

Just then, the door opened with a soft creak. Aglaea entered the room without a moment of hesitation.

“Hello, Phainon. How are you feeling?” Aglaea asked, her voice entirely devoid of judgment. Yet, it carried an underlying weight, as if she already knew he was not okay and was hiding something.

Before he could scramble to think of an excuse, Mydei stepped forward, his heavy boots cutting through the suffocating tension. He didn’t directly interrupt Aglaea, but his sharp, impatient tone left no room for pleasantries.

“Enough,” Mydei said, his eyebrows furrowed as his gaze locked onto Phainon. “Just tell us what happened before then. You started hyperventilating, then fainted right in front of us. You kept murmuring something under your breath, but we couldn't understand a single word. What made you panic like that, Deliverer?”

Phainon liked to think he was a good judge of character; he could always instinctively understand what people wanted from him—he wasn’t sure how he knew that, but he did. Yet right now, he couldn't understand a single thing about what the people in this room wanted from him.

Realistically, he knew they were his friends and comrades; he could feel that bond. But then what were the things he saw when he passed out? A dream, or the past? He didn’t know for sure, but he could guess. The horrors he had witnessed felt entirely real. Perhaps not in the exact way they played out, but the core of it was real.

“I don’t know,” he said, his own brow furrowing. “I just felt very lightheaded all of a sudden and couldn't breathe.”

Mydei stared at Phainon, his eyes showing he knew perfectly well that it was a lie, but he seemed to be waiting for a better opportunity to push for the truth.

"Whatever," Mydei grunted, breaking the heavy silence. "Just say you're as useless as always." To anyone else, the remark would have sounded downright cruel.

But Phainon knew better; he couldn't logically explain how, but deep down, he could feel the hidden current of worry beneath the blonde prince's harsh words. Mydei was concerned—he just didn't know how else to show it.

Aglaea stepped forward, looking down at Phainon as she assessed his condition. Apparently satisfied that he was stable enough for now, she took a step back.

“I would like to see you as soon as you're able, Phainon. We have important matters to discuss. Take your time to recover, but remember, the past rarely likes to be kept waiting.”

With that, she turned and exited the room, moving as elegantly as always.

While Aglaea had been speaking, Mydei had shifted to stand next to the door. He kept his eyes fixed intently on Phainon, as if trying to figure out exactly what to do in this predicament.

Phainon closed his eyes, secretly wishing that whatever storm was coming would at least arrive quietly. He was entirely, utterly exhausted—not just in body, but in a part of his soul he couldn't even remember.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 7: wounds of the mind
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

"And before you even think to say you’re fine, know that if I hear those words, I'm going to toss you out the window."

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

“When did you get that wound?” Mydei scrunched his nose, lifting his eyebrows. “There wasn't a wound like that when Hyacine treated you before—I was there. So, you were always with someone, and I was also there... How and where did you get a wound like that?”

At first, he didn't understand what Mydei was talking about. Then it hit him. Mydei was talking about the wound on his shoulder which had appeared from his 'not-so-dream’. How could he explain that while he was unconscious, he got that wound inside a dream? Would anyone even believe that? Well, only one way to find out.

“Uhm so, remember when I passed out six hours ago?” Phainon grimaced. “Well, I don't remember having a wound like that either. Is it possible to get injured in a dream?”

Mydei looked at him like he was trying very hard not to kill him right then and there, oops. He had already told them he didn't remember anything from his 'not-so-dream’, and now he couldn't just go back on his word. He couldn't just expose his own lie.

Unlike Mydei, Hyacine was actually taking him seriously and wasn't debating whether to kill him or not.

“It isn't unheard of, but... how could that possibly be, though?” Hyacine mumbled to herself. “I need to speak with Lady Aglaea first. Rest here, Phainon. I don't want to see you outside of that bed when I come back, alright?” Hyacine smiled, but it didn't reach her eyes. She then stood up and left the room without turning back. Now he was alone with Mydei… He didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

Phainon tried to smooth the conversation over. “Soo, how are you doing..?” Phainon’s face didn't change, but he was facepalming internally. Mydei didn't outwardly react to his words, as if he couldn't believe he just heard such a dumb question. Then his face reddened with anger.

“Are you serious right now?!” Phainon was also asking that question to himself. “How am I doing? How am I doing?! I'm not the one who is in a hospital bed right now! Can you be serious for like five minutes? The things that happened to you—none of them are normal! You can see that, right?” Mydei was far angrier than Phainon thought.

“Okay, okay, wait. I'm sorry, okay? I just panicked. I don't know what’s happening either, and I don't have any of my memories. The things that I saw don't explain anything, and I am so, so tired.” Phainon slumped his shoulders, the sheer exhaustion finally catching up to him.

Mydei was silently watching him, trying to understand him. Mydei opened his mouth as if he was going to ask a question, but he stopped, probably thinking better of it. He sat in the chair next to Phainon's bed without saying anything.

“How do you feel right now, Deliverer? Just be honest.” Mydei tried to meet him in the middle, offering a compromise. Phainon lifted his head, looking directly into Mydei's eyes. He opened his mouth to say he was fine, but Mydei probably sensed that, cause he didn't even have the time to say the word ‘I’ before Mydei cut him off, saying, “And before you even think to say you’re fine, know that if I hear those words, I'm going to toss you out the window. So, think again.” Mydei crossed his arms, daring Phainon to say the words. Phainon was a brave person, or so he liked to think. But now, he questioned whether he was brave or stupid.

So Phainon did the only reasonable thing. “I'm feeling... good?” Mydei didn't waste his time standing up. Just as he was about to grab Phainon, Phainon relented. “Okay, okay! By the Titans, you need to learn how to take a joke! You can't live like this.” Phainon tried to change the subject, but seeing Mydei wasn't backing off, he added, “I mostly feel okay—don't look at me like that, I'm not done—my whole body aches and I don't feel like moving at all, but other than that, it's... okay. It's okay.”

Mydei searched his face, as if he was trying to determine if he was telling the truth. Then he must have found no deception, because he nodded and said, “What about your shoulder then? And don't try to lie saying you don't know, we both know that was utter nonsense. So, tell me.” Phainon wasn't sure what he was supposed to say to Mydei. As much as he wanted to lie, he was oddly certain that telling the truth wouldn't put him in a difficult position—though where that sudden surge of trust came from, he had no idea.

Phainon eventually gave up on these thoughts and decided to accept his fate. He looked at Mydei and asked, "This stays between us, got it? You can't tell anyone else. Do you promise?" Mydei raised his eyebrows at first, caught off guard by the question. Then, looking deeply into Phainon's eyes with a reassuring gaze, he said, "I promise."

Hearing Mydei say "I promise," a sudden sense of relief washed over him from somewhere unknown, and he decided to tell him the truth without leaving out a single detail.

“In my dream, it was either a younger version of me or just a figment of my imagination—I’m not entirely sure, but he looked like me as a child. He touched me right in the middle of my destroyed village. At first, I tried to save him, thinking he was a stranger, but then he touched my shoulder, and that’s where this mark came from. He told me that I could never save anyone, that everything was my fault. Why would my subconscious say something like that to me when I don't even remember anything? I saw something else before that too, but... I don't want to talk about it right now. Simply put, whatever I saw in that dream bled into reality, and I have no idea what to do about it.

What are the things I heard in that dream supposed to mean? What am I supposed to do? And I can't just trust everyone, just like not everyone can trust me. I have no idea what's real and what's a lie anymore, and my head is a complete mess.”

Mydei looked as though he certainly hadn't expected such an answer when he asked about the wound. Then again, who could have possibly expected a response like that? It was probably the most natural reaction anyone could have. Mydei was surprised, yet there was no fear in his eyes, nor did he look the least bit suspicious of him, despite everything Phainon had just confessed.

Mydei sighed softly and said, “Whatever you saw in that dream... none of it matters. Because you are a person capable of making your own decisions and choosing what to do next through your own actions. As for the things you saw... you've always been someone who blamed himself for everything anyway. That might have something to do with it. A wound from a dream manifesting in real life is strange, I'll admit, but everything has an explanation.”

“So... you believe me?” Phainon asked. “I mean, after everything I’ve told you... even I don't believe it. How can you just accept what I said without questioning a single thing?”

Mydei stared deeply into Phainon's eyes, waiting until he was certain Phainon was looking right back at him before he spoke.

“Phainon, you might be a good warrior, but you were never a good storyteller. I don't think for a second you could pull a tale like that out of thin air in two seconds. And you're not a liar. At least, not unless you absolutely have to be. That's how I know.”

Phainon stared at Mydei as if he couldn't believe what he was hearing, and let out a deep breath. Then Phainon asked, "Do you know when I'll be discharged from the hospital?"

"You're stuck here until at least tonight," Mydei replied with a subtle, teasing smirk. "We'll figure out the rest later. Now get some sleep; we'll talk in more detail when I come back."

Hearing this, Phainon collapsed back onto the bed. They said their goodbyes, and as Phainon drifted off to sleep, he was left wondering how Mydei could possibly trust him this much.

Chapter End Notes
